title: Interleaved shadow->canary promote coordinator with session anchoring and manual-hash override
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: we observed late-stage regressions when promoting shadow traffic directly to canary lanes for sessionful workloads (chat, streaming). Current promote paths cause partial session rebinds and user-visible replays under load. This PR introduces an Interleaved Shadow->Canary Promote Coordinator that: 1) anchors session affinity during the promote window, 2) performs per-session deterministic hash stepping to interleave shadow requests into canary lanes for gradual promotion, 3) exposes a manual-hash override to force deterministic promotion for debugging and fast rollbacks, and 4) integrates telemetry gates (latency/error/fidelity) to stop/resume promotion automatically.

Summary of changes: single logical feature implemented across coordinator, tests, docs, and an operator runbook. The coordinator is implemented as a non-blocking controller that works with existing traffic-slicing primitives and the session-store sidecar. It intentionally keeps the fast path zero-copy for opt-in stateless flows.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-6821)
- [x] Implementation of coordinator and session anchoring
- [x] Unit and integration tests for session-preservation and interleaving
- [x] Telemetry gates with configurable thresholds (latency p95, fidelity regression, error-rate)
- [x] Operator docs and rollback playbook added
- [x] End-to-end staging run with synthetic chat workload

Design notes: Coordinator attaches a transient promotion binding to session metadata (TTL-bound) and uses a two-phase interleave: pilot (0.5-2% sessions) then ramp (geometric by session hash space). Manual-hash override allows engineering to pin specific hash prefixes for diagnostics; the override is only allowed for orgs with operator-level access and requires audit log entries. Telemetry gates run in a separate evaluation thread and post halt/resume commands to the coordinator. The implementation opts for eventual consistency and idempotent control messages to avoid stalls.

Testing: Added deterministic integration harness (test/integration/interleaved_promote_harness.go) that simulates 10k active sessions with streaming tokens. New tests cover: session continuity across promote, manual-hash override behavior, rollback after fidelity regression, and gate-triggered halt. One flaky test was stabilized by replacing wall-clock sleeps with simulated time in harness.

Rollout plan: Canary in staging for 24h -> incremental enablement on non-critical orgs (2% -> 10% sessions over 6h) -> monitor p95 latency, fidelity delta, and error-rate for 2x baseline window -> full enable. Operators can trigger immediate revert via the runbook command (scripts/runbook/rollback_interleaved_promote.sh).

Notes: This PR does not change public API surface; config is gated behind a feature-flag (feature.interleaved_promote). Security review: manual-hash override audited and requires RBAC scope 'operator.promote.override'.
